problem_text:
A shipping terminal must devise a replenishment and storage schedule for a critical fuel additive over an operational window spanning 16 weeks.  
The starting stock at the commencement of the planning interval is 26 thousand liters.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 16 \), the terminal may request a delivery from its supplier, where the shipment volume must be between 13 and 59 thousand liters.  
Every delivery, once dispatched, requires a 2‑week transit time before it becomes available for consumption or for augmenting the terminal’s reserves.  
The weekly consumption of the additive is predetermined as follows:  

* Week 1: 52 thousand liters  
* Week 2: 18 thousand liters  
* Week 3: 43 thousand liters  
* Week 4: 51 thousand liters  
* Week 5: 41 thousand liters  
* Week 6: 29 thousand liters  
* Week 7: 34 thousand liters  
* Week 8: 44 thousand liters  
* Week 9: 44 thousand liters  
* Week 10: 14 thousand liters  
* Week 11: 15 thousand liters  
* Week 12: 48 thousand liters  
* Week 13: 56 thousand liters  
* Week 14: 41 thousand liters  
* Week 15: 58 thousand liters  
* Week 16: 10 thousand liters  

Supply deficits are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption in a given week is permanently lost and will not be recovered later.  
Throughout the 16‑week horizon, all quantities—including shipments, stock, and shortfalls—may be treated as continuous values. The physical storage tanks at the terminal can hold at most 52 thousand liters at any moment.  
The aggregate expense comprises three elements: a procurement cost of 3 per thousand liters ordered; a storage cost of 1 per thousand liters held over from one week to the next; and a penalty of 6 per thousand liters of unmet weekly consumption.  
The objective is to establish the optimal delivery quantity for each week and to monitor the ensuing stock and deficit levels, so as to minimize the total incurred cost.
